scope: Independent literature prior-source survey for the low-troposphere aerosol increment (task-prior-source-survey). Purpose: evidence collection and coverage assessment only — no default change, no new-default proposal, no decision. Three justification lanes are evaluated on their own evidence: (1) fixed higher prior, (2) documented range/distribution, (3) keep current default with the standing gap. Values here are collected independently of the four eclipse events; they never enter the model default. Coverage is not justification: a source covering a retrieval-spec dimension is recorded as covered/partial, never as justifying a specific default value.
source_convention: Pinned-source contract inherited from validation/results/extinction_gap_diagnosis/prior_parameters.json: every numeric value carries a pinned source with file_name + sha256 (64-hex, verified against the downloaded bytes) + printed location (page/table); rows or fields that could not be obtained carry status unavailable + a search_log.md pointer, never values from memory. Extension for non-PDF sources (online databases / data products): pin the exported/downloaded byte artefact (sha256 + bytes) plus the retrieval URL and the access date; an interactive source from which no bytes can be exported is recorded unavailable with its search trail — a bare URL without pinned bytes is not a valid source. Downloaded bytes are cached in outputs/prior_source_survey/raw/ (git-ignored); the repository commits only these JSON/md records, and anyone can re-download and verify via the recorded sha256.

retrieval_spec_reference.note: The dimensions being surveyed are referenced by json-path into this committed product (see coverage_matrix.json); the sha256 is recorded at coverage-matrix build time, not here, so this file does not drift when the matrix is built.

sources.name: opac1998_bams_paper_mpg_copy
sources.role: OPAC canonical paper (secondary byte artifact; the repo-pinned canonical copy lives in prior_parameters.json contract, sha256 68a20ba9..., 121916 bytes, hosted at lweb.cfa.harvard.edu). This MPG-repository copy independently re-downloads the same paper for the survey; all printed locations in this survey cite the paper's printed pagination.
sources.citation: Hess, M., Koepke, P., & Schult, I. (1998). Optical Properties of Aerosols and Clouds: The Software Package OPAC. Bull. Am. Meteorol. Soc., 79(5), 831-844.

source.location: whole paper; Sec. 3 (dataset, 61 wavelengths 0.25-40 um, eight RH classes), Table 1c (printed p. 837), Table 3 (printed p. 840), Table 4-5 (printed p. 841-843)

sources.name: opac1998_component_data_files
sources.role: The per-component per-RH optical-property ASCII files of the OPAC 1998 (v3.1) distribution - the dataset whose absence caused the 11 `unavailable` RH-variant rows in prior_parameters.json. The four water-uptaking components (WASO water-soluble, SUSO sulfate droplets, SSAM/SSCM sea salt acc./coa.) carry the humidity growth axis used by humidity_growth.json.
sources.citation: OPAC v3.1 (1998) component data files, distributed per Hess, Koepke & Schult (1998); redistributed by GEISA/AERIS (portal geisa.aeris-data.fr/opac, which documents the classic BAMS98 dataset), recovered via web.archive.org captures of the ESPRI distribution servers.
sources.version_verification: Identified as the original 1998 dataset, not OPAC 2015: (1) each file contains the 61-wavelength grid 0.25-40 um exactly as described in BAMS98 Sec. 2; (2) dry-state microphysical parameters in the file headers match BAMS98 Table 1c verbatim (WASO sigma 2.24, dry rmod 0.0212 um; SUSO sigma 2.03, dry rmod 0.0695 um; checked on every retrieved file); (3) native OPAC ASCII format (header + 9-column optical table normalized ext.nor=1 at 0.55 um + scattering-angle x wavelength phase function). Caveat recorded honestly: no independent Mie-recomputation was performed; identification rests on these three structural/parameter checks plus the documented GEISA portal provenance (the '2011'/'2015' strings are GEISA redistribution path labels, not dataset versions; GEISA also publishes a separate genuine OPAC 2015 entry which was NOT used).

missing_files.reason: not captured by web.archive.org on either ESPRI host (404 from wayback for all 12, tried across 2022/2023/2024/2025 timestamps); direct ESPRI download impossible from this network (TCP connect OK, TLS handshake times out on both aeris-geisa.ipsl.fr and cds-espri.ipsl.upmc.fr); FlexAOD mirror (bundles data/gads/optdat) under server maintenance (HTTP maintenance page); see search_log.md entries W1.3-W1.7
missing_files.impact: RH growth curves remain constructible from the retrieved files: SUSO has 00/70/80/95/98/99 (6 of 8), WASO has 00/50/70/99 (4 of 8 incl. both endpoints), SSAM has all 8 (both endpoints), SSCM has 00/50/80/90/95 (5 of 8; the high-RH endpoint classes 98/99 are missing, so no SSCM dry->99% growth is asserted). Full dry->99% endpoint pairs exist only for SUSO/WASO/SSAM. Missing are mid-RH points for WASO (80/90/95/98) and SUSO (50/90), SSCM 70/98/99, plus 3 non-hygroscopic components.

sources.name: aeronet_v3_gsfc_2011_lev20
sources.role: Mid-latitude (39.0 N) site AOD time series, Level 2.0 (cloud-cleared, quality assured, pre/post-field calibration applied), calendar year 2011, all retrievals. Serves the AOD-distribution coverage dimension: near-550nm channels (500/551/560 nm) directly comparable to the retrieval-spec AOD550 pool without wavelength conversion, and 440-870/440-675/500-870 Angstrom pairs cover the alpha dimensions. Independent of the four eclipse events.
sources.citation: AERONET Version 3 Direct Sun product, site GSFC (NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, 38.9925 N, 76.8398 W, 87 m), AOD Level 2.0, year 2011, retrieved via the AERONET Data Download (Version 3 Direct Sun) web service. Data use per aeronet.gsfc.nasa.gov data usage guidelines (cite the site and PI: PI=Pawan_Gupta_and_Elena_Lind as recorded in the file header).

source.location: CSV: header lines 1-5 (product/level/PI declaration), then one row per retrieval; columns AOD_500nm / AOD_551nm / AOD_560nm / AOD_440nm etc. (-999 = missing), 440-870 / 440-675 / 500-870 Angstrom_Exponent, Site_Latitude/Longitude/Elevation

sources.name: dubovik2002_aeronet_types
sources.role: AERONET-based aerosol-type optical property climatology at 12 worldwide sites: per-site observed AOD ranges (tau at 440 nm for urban/biomass; tau at 1020 nm for dust/oceanic rows), Angstrom exponent ranges, SSA. Serves: AOD-distribution coverage (site-level observed ranges incl. clean-marine low end at Lanai) and alpha-envelope comparison (alpha computed on the 440/870 pair - different pair than the spec's blue/visible pairs; recorded as caveat).
sources.citation: Dubovik, O., Holben, B. N., Eck, T. F., Smirnov, A., Kaufman, Y. J., King, M. D., Tanre, D., & Slutsker, I. (2002). Variability of Absorption and Optical Properties of Key Aerosol Types Observed in Worldwide Locations. J. Atmos. Sci., 59, 590-608.

source.location: Table 1 (PDF pp. 44/48 of the GISS-hosted preprint layout), rows 'Urban/Industrial & Mixed' (GSFC 0.1<=tau440<=1.0, mean 0.24; Creteil 0.1-0.9; Mexico City 0.1-1.8; Maldives 0.1-0.7), 'Desert Dust & Oceanic' (Lanai/Hawaii 0.01<=tau1020<=0.2, mean 0.04; Cape Verde 0.1-2.0), alpha ranges per site (urban 1.0-2.5, oceanic 0-1.55)

sources.name: winker2013_calipso_3d
sources.role: CALIPSO lidar global climatology of aerosol vertical distribution and AOD (532 nm). Serves: layer-geometry context via the H63 column statistic (altitude below which 63% of column AOD lies; equals the exponential scale height only for an UNTRUNCATED profile, so comparison against the spec's 10-km-truncated layer requires the conversion in coverage_matrix.json derived_comparisons, which crosses definitions and does not certify or exclude the profile) and clean-ocean AOD levels. Values read from figures are approximate figure reads, flagged as such.
sources.citation: Winker, D. M., Tackett, J. L., Getzewich, B. J., Liu, Z., Vaughan, M. A., & Rogers, R. R. (2013). The global 3-D distribution of tropospheric aerosols: a view from CALIPSO. Atmos. Chem. Phys., 13, 3345-3361.

source.location: Sec. 5 (H63 metric definition, printed p. 3351-3352); Fig. 9 (printed p. 3352): seasonal mean H63 maps, colorbar 0-5 km, oceans ~1-2 km, most land 1.5-3 km, max ~4.5-5 km over deserts/elevated source regions, polar high values stated spurious in text; Fig. 10 (same page): seasonal mean AOD 532 nm maps, ocean background ~0.05-0.1, land source regions up to 0.9-1.0

sources.figure_read_caveat: H63 and AOD values quoted from Fig. 9/10 are read off published color maps (approximate, bin resolution ~0.5 km / ~0.1 AOD); no tabulated numeric values exist in the paper text.
